![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/cf44412afd6f2a8eaab468676b4f6a9828f5000eec287234f9834a41e6816d5a.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=20x$ for $z\le 0,$ shown above.
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$  represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $10$ centered at $(10,0,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=20x$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =20x \\ {\rho }^{2} & =20\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -20\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =20\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/165ed50d8f94f3b896f4d19647fb514f544221872a6df241a6ab6c3797bbd698.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 20\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{20\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
